source_refs.note: Topic printed 4.1.2.1 Stack Operations (PDF 96-97, printed 93-94); the number 4.1.2.1 is repeated. Figure 4.2 (stack of books photo) is replaced by the original diagram. MCQ 3 is answered.

items: Push: add an item to the top. In Python a list is used as the stack and append() pushes.
Pop: remove the item from the top with the list's pop().

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
stack_of_books = []
stack_of_books.append("Book A")
stack_of_books.append("Book B")
stack_of_books.append("Book C")
print("Stack:", stack_of_books)        # Book A, Book B, Book C
top_book = stack_of_books.pop()
print("Removed book:", top_book)       # Book C
print("Stack now:", stack_of_books)    # Book A, Book B

blocks.caption: Lists, stacks, queues and postfix evaluation (original diagram after topics 4.1.1 to 4.1.5).
blocks.long_description: A list keeps items in order with indexes from 0, so Plates is at index 3, and items can be inserted, appended, removed or found. A stack of books is used only from the top: pushing adds Book C on top of Book B and Book A, and popping removes Book C first, the last one added. A queue serves from the front and adds at the back: Ahmed, who came first, is served first, and Sara joins behind Ali. To evaluate 3 4 5 * +, the numbers are pushed one by one; the * pops 5 and 4 and pushes 20, then + pops 20 and 3 and pushes the answer 23.

blocks.text: Like a stack of books on a desk, you can only add a book on top or take the top book off. Stacks are also used in depth-first search (DFS) to manage the nodes to explore in LIFO order (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Which operation removes an item from the top of a stack (MCQ 3)?

items: push = append(), pop = pop(); pushing A, B, C then popping returns C.
